messages:
carla: Heads-up — EU pool saturated for the past 40m. Ops alert from infra-bot showed 95% GPU util on shard-eu-3 while overall scheduling backlog is growing. A few tenants with long-lived sessions and big KV caches.

ben: seeing it too, thanks. Is this the sticky affinity change we rolled last week?

carla: I suspect sticky sessions + long prompt context + embedding pipelines that keep KV alive. infra-bot shows top tenants: tenant_x (60% of KV), tenant_y (20%), tenant_z (10%).

darren: if tenant_x keeps pinning shards with warm KV, they blow through shared pool capacity. We need quick mitigation — can we soft-evict idle kv or enforce per-tenant kv caps?

alice: agree. Short-term: add an admission throttle for tenants based on their "active_kv_bytes" + inflight tokens. Medium-term: move heavy KV users to dedicated pools or encourage caching hints.

ben: wrote a quick naive admission policy sketch: 
```
# per-request admission check pseudocode
if tenant.active_kv_bytes > KV_SOFT_CAP and tenant.inflight_qps > QPS_THRESHOLD:
    apply_backoff(tenant, method='token-leaky', tokens=compute_tokens(tenant))
elif pool.util > POOL_HIGH_WM:
    route_to_fallback_model_or_queue(tenant.request)
else:
    accept_request()
```
This keeps long-lived sessions but throttles new inflight work from noisy tenants.

carla: love the pseudocode. Two operational notes: 1) KV_SOFT_CAP must be adaptive per model & seq-length distribution; 2) backoff should be cooperative (HTTP 429 + Retry-After + estimated queue position) so clients can choose to retry or downgrade.

darren: also add a short TTL eviction for KV entries after N seconds of inactivity. If a tenant needs persistently warm KV, route them to dedicated capacity automatically (offer migration).

alice: on metrics: we need tenant_kv_bytes, tenant_seq_dist (p50/p95), tenant_inflight_ops, pool_queued_count. Without those, any controller will be blind. Can we add them to the next infra scrape?

carla: ops-bot: create incident ticket for EU shard-eu-3 saturation and mark as P2. Add a follow-up to add tenant_kv_bytes metric.

ops-bot: Incident created -> INC-2026; assigned to eng-platform and eng-infra.

ben: quick sim numbers I ran locally: if tenant_kv_bytes cap = 40% of pool, overall tail latency drops 30% in bursts, cost stays ~flat because we're avoiding preemptive retries.

darren: implementation plan suggestion:
- short term (1 day): add soft admission controller with token bucket tied to tenant_kv_bytes + inflight; return 429 w/ Retry-After
- medium (1-2 weeks): implement ephemeral affinity (evict sticky for low-use sessions) + KV TTL + routing hint to dedicated
- long term (quarter): fairness score that weights tenant by business tier + historical fairness credit; automatic offers to migrate to Dedicated when sustained heavy KV usage

carla: decision: go with short-term plan now. Ben/Darren pick up admission controller PR, Alice add metrics to scrape pipeline today, I'll update runbook and communicate to support.

ben: I can take the short-term PR. Will open RFC branch and ping for review.

alice: adding metrics now. Dashboards requested: per-tenant KV mem, per-shard util, backpressure events.

carla: thanks. Also update docs for client SDKs to handle 429 gracefully (Retry-After + degrade to smaller context). I'll notify success/customer teams about potential transient throttling for EU. :wave:

ben: tagging @darren for PR once ready.

darren: will do. Low-code experiment: consider giving tenants a small 'warm-window' credit so a single warmup burst isn't penalized, but repeated warmups are throttled.

carla: noted. We'll iterate after telemetry arrives.

(reacts: :thumbsup: from alice, :rocket: from ben)
